The balanced heads trade raw per-criterion accuracy for recall on rare criterion values; binary-concept F1 (row above) is the metric the promotion was selected on.

rows.metric: Classifier-alone sensitivity at the union's own specificity (M1)
rows.source_path: roc_curve_data.json promoted_classifier_roc.points (max sensitivity_tpr at specificity >= 0.6973); reviewer finding M1
rows.note: Not a base-vs-promoted comparison (base_arm left null on purpose). At the SAME specificity the union rule operates at (0.6973), the promoted classifier ALONE -- just by lowering its threshold -- reaches sensitivity 0.9307, ABOVE the union rule's own 0.8614 (delta shown here is vs the union row, not vs a base arm). So the union's +0.1188 sensitivity gain over the base arm (row above) is a gain relative to the classifier's ARGMAX operating point only, not relative to what the classifier's own ROC can already achieve by moving its threshold. The criteria path's honest value is evidential/complementary (criterion-level audit trail, human-adjudicated disagreement -- see the Venn/complementarity numbers elsewhere), not an incremental melanoma-detection gain beyond the classifier's own ROC.
Promoted CI95 [0.4317, 0.638], base CI95 [0.4734, 0.6598] -- the promoted CI covers the base point estimate, so the dip is not resolvable at n=395 (dual-reported in the source artifact, not hidden).

Same underlying cause as the union-specificity cost above: the balanced criteria heads disagree with the classifier more often, which is also the mechanism the sensitivity gain runs through -- a safety/efficiency trade, not a pure regression.
Largest v2-vs-current gain of the three grounding scopes.
